title: Kenyan Tamarind Glazed Fish
community: Swahili — the celebratory coastal fish dish
author: Chef Amina Hassan
desc: Kenyan Tamarind Glazed Fish — whole fish marinated in tamarind, garlic, and spices, grilled over charcoal with repeated tamarind glaze applications until the skin is magnificently lacquered, sweet-sour, and fragrant. The showpiece fish dish of the Swahili coast celebration table.
longDesc: Tamarind glazed fish is the coastal celebration fish dish — where everyday tamarind fish is a simple sauce preparation, this celebration version uses the tamarind as a glaze applied layer by layer during grilling, building a magnificent lacquered surface on a whole fish. The result is visually stunning and flavourfully extraordinary.
ingredients: 1 whole large fish (1—1.5 kg) — snapper, barracuda, or kingfish
steps: Score the fish deeply on both sides — 4—5 diagonal cuts through to the bone.
Mix the tamarind glaze ingredients. Divide into two portions — one for marinating, one for basting.
Rub the marinade portion all over and into the scored cuts. Marinate 1 hour.
Grill fish for 8—10 minutes per side, basting with the second portion of glaze every 3 minutes.
The fish is done when the skin is deeply lacquered and slightly charred at the edges.
Final baste immediately off the grill for maximum glaze shine.
Serve whole on a large platter.
chefTips: The multiple glaze applications are what create the lacquered effect — do not rush this.
Keep heat medium-low — the sugar in the tamarind burns quickly over high heat.
Score deeply to allow the marinade to penetrate the flesh.
commonMistakes: High heat — burns the glaze before the fish is cooked.
Single application of glaze — does not build the lacquered effect.
cookingScience: Repeated applications of the tamarind-sugar glaze build up successive Maillard-caramelised layers. Each layer dries and caramelises before the next is applied, creating a thick, complex, multi-layered surface with deeper flavour than a single application.
sustainabilityTips: Choose whole fish from sustainable coastal fisheries.
storage: Best eaten fresh from the grill.
reheating: Warm in oven — do not microwave.
culturalNote: Tamarind glazed whole fish is the showpiece of the Swahili coastal celebration table — its glistening, lacquered surface communicates the care and skill of the cook and the importance of the occasion.
